title: Logarithmic Independence for Local Permutations
summary: The stronger conjecture is refuted, while this weakened logarithmic-independence version is not refuted by the paper’s counterexample; its pseudorandomness implication remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For a randomized permutation $P:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^n$ in which each output bit depends on only a constant number of input bits, determine whether the $T$-fold composition $P^T$ is a pseudorandom permutation whenever $P^T$ is negligibly far from $\log(n)$-wise independence. This conjectured implication is a weakened form of a refuted stronger conjecture: the known counterexample distinguishes a constant number of invariants using only a constant number of wires, while that approach does not apply when $\omega(1)$ invariants must be maintained. Thus, the unresolved task is to establish or refute the stated pseudorandomness implication under the constant-locality condition. [S1]

scope.domain: Mathematical foundations of pseudorandomness, limited independence, and randomized permutations with constant locality.
assumptions: P is a randomized permutation from n-bit strings to n-bit strings.
Each output bit depends on only a constant number of input bits.
The T-fold composition P^T is negligibly far from log(n)-wise independence.
parameters: n, the input and output bit length
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the stated implication to pseudorandomness holds or can be refuted under the constant-locality condition.

citations.label: When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness

progress.summary: The source presents this explicitly as Conjecture 3, a weakened variant of a stronger conjecture not refuted by the paper’s counterexample. It notes that the counterexample’s constant-invariant strategy does not extend to maintaining ω(1)-many invariants.
citation_labels: Jesko Dujmovic et al., When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness
